crack a joke: To make the nervous students relax, the teacher decided to crack a joke before handing out the test.
為了讓緊張的學生放鬆，老師在發考卷前決定說個笑話。
crack down on crime: The city hired more police officers to crack down on crime in the area around the train station.
市政府增聘警力，以打擊火車站周邊地區的犯罪。
crack under pressure: Even the best players can crack under pressure when thousands of fans are shouting during the final game.
在決賽中數千名球迷大聲吶喊時，即使是最好的球員也可能在壓力下崩潰。
crack a case: After ten years of searching, the detective finally cracked a case and arrested the thief who stole the paintings.
經過十年的搜查，警探終於破案，逮捕了偷畫的竊賊。
crack a smile: The guard looked serious all day, but he cracked a smile when the little girl waved at him.
那名警衛整天表情嚴肅，但當小女孩向他揮手時，他露出了微笑。
craft a speech: The class leader spent the whole weekend trying to craft a speech for the graduation ceremony.
班長花了整個週末為畢業典禮精心撰寫演講稿。
craft a strategy: The coach sat down with his players to craft a strategy for beating the strongest team in the league.
教練和球員們坐下來，擬定擊敗聯盟最強隊伍的策略。
carefully crafted: Every wooden toy in this shop is carefully crafted by hand, so each one takes several days to make.
這家店的每個木製玩具都是手工精心打造的，所以每個都要花好幾天製作。
the market crashed: Many families lost their savings when the market crashed and stock prices fell by half in one week.
股市崩盤、股價一週內跌了一半時，許多家庭失去了積蓄。
the computer crashed: I lost my whole report because the computer crashed before I had a chance to save it.
我還來不及存檔電腦就當機了，所以整份報告都不見了。
crash a party: A group of strangers tried to crash a party at our house, so my dad asked them to leave.
一群陌生人想要不請自來參加我們家的派對，所以我爸請他們離開。
crash into a wall: The driver fell asleep at the wheel, and his car crashed into a wall beside the highway.
駕駛開車時睡著了，他的車撞上了公路旁的牆。
crash on the sofa: After the long trip, I was so tired that I just crashed on the sofa without taking a shower.
長途旅行後，我累到沒洗澡就直接倒在沙發上睡了。
traffic crawled: Because of the heavy rain and an accident ahead, traffic crawled along the highway for two hours.
因為大雨和前方的車禍，公路上車流緩慢地爬行了兩個小時。
crawl with tourists: In summer, the old streets of Jiufen crawl with tourists taking photos and buying snacks.
夏天時，九份老街擠滿了拍照和買小吃的觀光客。
crawl back: After quitting his job in anger, Sam had to crawl back to his old boss and beg for another chance.
氣憤辭職之後，山姆只好灰溜溜回到老闆那裡，求他再給一次機會。
make one's skin crawl: The sound of nails scratching a blackboard can make my skin crawl every time I hear it.
指甲刮黑板的聲音每次都令我起雞皮疙瘩。
credit someone with: Many historians credit Thomas Edison with making the electric light practical for ordinary homes.
許多歷史學家把讓電燈得以在一般家庭使用的功勞歸功於愛迪生。
be credited to one's account: The bank said the refund will be credited to your account within five working days.
銀行說退款會在五個工作天內入帳到你的帳戶。
credit the success to: The team captain chose to credit the success to the hard work of every player, not just himself.
隊長把成功歸於每位球員的努力，而不只是他自己。
take credit for: It is unfair when a manager tries to take credit for the ideas that his workers came up with.
主管把員工想出的點子據為己功（居功），是很不公平的。
prices creep up: Every year, food prices creep up a little, so the same lunch now costs much more than before.
每年食物的物價都會悄悄上漲一點，所以同樣的午餐現在比以前貴多了。
creep into one's mind: As the exam date got closer, doubts began to creep into her mind about whether she had studied enough.
隨著考試日期逼近，她是否讀得夠多的疑慮開始悄悄浮現心頭。
creep up on someone: The cat likes to creep up on someone quietly and then jump onto their lap.
這隻貓喜歡悄悄接近人，然後跳到他們腿上。
cripple the economy: Experts warned that a long war could cripple the economy and leave millions of people without jobs.
專家警告，長期戰爭可能重創經濟，讓數百萬人失業。
crippling debt: After borrowing too much to open a restaurant, the couple struggled with crippling debt for years.
為了開餐廳借了太多錢後，這對夫妻多年來一直苦於沉重債務。
cripple the system: A powerful computer virus could cripple the system that controls the city's traffic lights.
一個強大的電腦病毒可能癱瘓控制全市紅綠燈的系統。
criticize the government: Thousands of people went online to criticize the government for raising electricity prices again.
數千人上網批評政府又調漲電價。
be criticized for: The mayor was criticized for spending too much public money on a park that few people use.
市長因為花太多公帑在一座很少人使用的公園上而遭批評。
criticize harshly: The coach did not criticize his players harshly after the loss; instead, he calmly showed them how to improve.
輸球後教練沒有嚴厲批評球員，反而冷靜地教他們如何進步。
